AnchorTerm.description:
One addend of a level anchor, in its own units.

Exactly one source (R16-6, 16 Oct 2026):

* ``by_scenario`` -- a value per world scenario, typed in the ARCHETYPE file. This is
  where level anchors live.
* ``value`` -- one value for every scenario, typed in the archetype file.
* ``path`` -- a dotted path into a company file (``{scenario}`` substituted,
  ``name[-1]`` indexes a list). Kept only where the number is the company's own
  typed input that its engine also reads (CSL's segment steady states).

path.description: Dotted path into the company file; ``{scenario}`` substituted; ``name[-1]`` indexes a list.
path.title: Path

value.description: One value for every scenario, in ``units``.
value.title: Value

AnchorTerm.title: AnchorTerm

ArchetypeRating.description:
Finer ordinal used in industry-archetype assessments (§7.4 v2 spec).

A superset of the three-point ``Rating`` with the ``x_to_y`` gradations and
``very_low`` that the newer archetype files (bank, biopharma) use for force
ratings, disruption severity and supply risk. Kept separate from ``Rating`` so
company-positioning fields stay on the strict three-point scale.
ArchetypeRating.title: ArchetypeRating

BankCostOfEquityAnchor.description:
The archetype-level Ke anchor and the peer evidence behind it.

Ranges are ``[low, high]`` and are validated as such: a reversed pair would
otherwise read as a range nobody could see was backwards.
BankCostOfEquityAnchor.title: BankCostOfEquityAnchor

Cet1Floor.description:
Regulatory CET1 floor, built from its named components.

``components_in_total`` must name exactly which components the stated floor
comprises, and the total is checked against those. It exists because a total
that silently disagrees with its own components is unreadable either way:
naming them turns "these do not add up" into "here is what adds up, and here
is what is deliberately outside it".

D-59, 16 September 2026. The declaration was originally used to carve the
countercyclical buffer OUT of the major-bank floor, which reconciled the
arithmetic and was wrong about APRA: APS 110 sets the CCyB by "extending the
range of the capital conservation buffer", so it sits inside the requirement.
The carve-out was papering over a larger error. ``regulatory_minimum`` held
the TOTAL capital minimum — Tier 1 plus Tier 2 — in a field measured on
CET1, where APRA's figure is the much lower CET1 PCR; and the conservation
buffer held the standardised figure where all four majors are on the IRB
approach and carry the higher one. Every component now shares the CET1
basis, and the stated floor is the sum of all four. What the file used to
call a floor was an OPERATING target wearing a floor's name, which is why
it looked plausible — see :class:`Cet1OperatingTarget`. The figures live in
the archetype YAML, sourced to APS 110 and APRA's own explainer.

The carve-out stays legal, because a buffer genuinely outside a headline
requirement is a real configuration in other jurisdictions. It is now a
thing a file has to mean rather than a thing it can drift into.
Cet1Floor.title: Cet1Floor

Cet1OperatingTarget.description:
The CET1 level a bank actually manages to, which is not the floor.

D-59. A payout rule does not bind at the regulatory floor. A bank manages to
a board-approved operating target and defends THAT — cutting distributions,
stopping a buyback — well before the floor is in sight, so the quantity that
governs behaviour in a dividend rule is the target, not the requirement. The
two were previously one field: an operating level stated as a floor, with a
separate ``cet1_management_buffer_typical`` to be added on top of it.
Anything reading both would have bound well above what APRA requires, and
above where any major has actually run.

``level`` is the absolute target, management buffer already inside it, not a
spread over the floor. The buffer is then *observed* as the gap to the floor
(:attr:`BankArchetype.implied_management_buffer`) rather than asserted
beside it — the same reason D-48 strikes capex and depreciation as a pair
and reads the gap.
Cet1OperatingTarget.title: Cet1OperatingTarget

ChainTermRole.description:
D-78: whether a growth-chain term survives into the scenario's equilibrium.

CURRENT_CYCLE terms are switched off for the equilibrium reading of the chain
(the reading that sets terminal growth, D-72) -- they take their declared
``equilibrium_value`` from the end of the explicit period. EQUILIBRIUM terms
stay at their typed value forever.
ChainTermRole.title: ChainTermRole

How non-royalty unit costs follow the primary commodity's real price (D-104, ruled
20 Oct 2026). Archetype-level; a company may override any field in its
``normalised_baseline.cost_price_link``.

elasticity_per_10pct.description: Percent move in non-royalty cash cost and sustaining capital for each 10% real move in the primary commodity price (1.5 = elasticity 0.15).
elasticity_per_10pct.title: Elasticity Per 10Pct

lag_years.description: Years between the price move and the cost response.
lag_years.title: Lag Years

cap_above_base_pct.description: Costs rise no more than this percent above the CPI-plus-escalator cost path.
cap_above_base_pct.title: Cap Above Base Pct

symmetric.description: Costs ease when the price falls (True) or only rise (False).
symmetric.title: Symmetric

CreditCycleAnchor.description: Through-cycle, peak and benign credit-loss anchors, in basis points.
CreditCycleAnchor.title: CreditCycleAnchor

DerivationMethod.description:
How a required macro driver's year-anchored path is obtained from a world scenario.

One entry per way the model has so far needed. Adding a method means adding
it here, in ``scripts/derive_macro_driver_paths.py`` (``METHODS``) and a test
in ``tests/test_macro_driver_paths.py`` -- nowhere else.
DerivationMethod.title: DerivationMethod

DisruptionVector.description: One disruption vector. Multiple per archetype (section 7.4).
DisruptionVector.title: DisruptionVector

FiveForces.description:
Porter's Five Forces, populated using the question bank in
design/frameworks/five_forces_questions.md.

Two naming generations coexist: the original ``new_entrants`` / ``substitutes``
(industrial archetypes) and the §7.4-v2 ``threat_of_new_entrants`` /
``threat_of_substitutes`` (+ optional ``rivalry_subforces``) used by the newer
bank and biopharma archetypes. Both are accepted; at least one form of each
force is expected.
FiveForces.title: FiveForces

GrowthChainTerm.description:
One coefficient of a company's growth chain and its role in equilibrium (D-78).

``path`` is the dotted path of the term under the company chain's ``shared``
block (e.g. ``industry_structure.volume_coefficient_a``). A current-cycle term
must say what value it takes once off (1.0 for a multiplier, 0.0 for an
additive term) and why; an equilibrium term carries neither.
GrowthChainTerm.title: GrowthChainTerm

InventoryBasis.description: How the producing inventory that sets mine life is counted (D-98 proposed).
InventoryBasis.title: InventoryBasis

LevelAnchor.description:
The level a derivation's path is calibrated to: one or more terms, summed.

R16-6 (16 Oct 2026): the anchors live in the ARCHETYPE file, as ``by_scenario`` /
``value`` terms. ``company`` and ``path`` remain for the one case where the level is
the company's own typed input that its engine also reads (CSL's three segment
steady states); ``company`` is then required, and only then. ``path`` alone is
shorthand for a single decimal company term. The company OFFSET is never part of
the anchor: the derived path is the industry's, and the offset stays in the
company layer (standing rule 1).
LevelAnchor.title: LevelAnchor
